text:
anita: Heads-up — Azure call tomorrow 10am PT with their account lead. We need final asks on committed capacity and the burst/fallback language.

michael_k: Copy. Main constraints: A100 availability in us-west2 and eu-west1, cross-region burst, and ability to shift unused commit between regions quarterly.

jin_ops: Also push for a baseline SLA on GPU allocation time (time to spin up reserved nodes) — last time warm pools took ~18m and that killed a canary. We should ask for a 10m target or credits.

lucas_fin: Finance question: Azure proposed $3.2M annual commitment for ~1,000 reserved A100-equivalent hours/day. We need to model 12 vs 36 month term. 12mo gives less discount but more flexibility. Thoughts?

anita: Let's enumerate negotiables: term length, per-region floor, burst credits, overage rates, early termination carve-outs, and applicability to Dedicated vs Hosted.

michael_k: Ask them to make burst capacity free up to X% of commit within the same billing period. If they won't, request a fixed overage rate cap (e.g., max 2x reserved rate).

jin_ops: For on-call impact: require monthly capacity reports + 24h notice on planned maintenance that affects reserved pools. If they do not give notice, we need service credits.

lucas_fin: Running quick calc: if reserved A100 rate = $2.10/hr (quoted), 1k hours/day -> ~$766.5k/month. 20% discount for a 36mo would be ~ $613k/mo. Need to check cashflow vs funding covenants.

anita: Good. Also confirm whether the commitment can be in $ (monetary) applied across compute + storage + egress, or limited to compute only. Our Legal prefers monetary commitments with a carveout for marketplace credits.

michael_k: Note: we should push for a clause that allows swapping instance families (e.g., A100 <-> H100-equivalent) at parity pricing if availability shifts. This avoids being stuck with unusable SKU.

jin_ops: Suggest adding an explicit "capacity guarantee" phrase: "Provider will maintain minimum available reserved capacity >= 95% of committed units in target regions or provide equivalent cross-region capacity within 2 hours." They may counter, but worth getting on paper.

lucas_fin: Also ask for billing audit access: raw invoice line items and per-region metering export. We need to reconcile usage vs commit daily for chargebacks.

anita: I'll draft the ask doc tonight. Agenda for the call: 1) commitments & term options 2) burst/overage mechanics 3) SKU swap flexibility 4) SLA & credits 5) reporting & audit.

michael_k: Can someone paste last quarter's peak utilization so finance can see risk? I remember a 48h spike during model training.

jin_ops: Pasted below:```
Peak usage week (Q4): average reserved utilization 78% daily, peak 96% for 48h, sustained at ~85% for heavy experiments. Unused commit trended ~22% baseline.```

lucas_fin: Perfect. That justifies a 12mo with a flexible right to reallocate quarterly. If Azure resists, push 24mo with review windows.

anita: @michael_k can you bring the draft term sheet? @lucas_fin can you prepare both a 12- and 36-month P&L scenario? jin_ops will list the SRE operational asks.

michael_k: On it. I'll also ask for explicit language on "dedicated pool preemption" — we can't accept preemption on reserved nodes unless compensated.

jin_ops: Also flag networking constraints: no single-region capacity ceilings that block cross-region failover. We need egress and VPC peering allowances for burst across regions without massive egress bills.

anita: If they offer marketplace credits as a partial concession, we should require them to apply to Dedicated compute charges, not just marketplace SKUs.

lucas_fin: One more: carve out a termination-for-convenience with 90d notice and prorated refund of unused commit after 90d. That gives us an exit if prices or performance worsen.

michael_k: OK — meeting prep looks solid. I'll record notes in the contract doc and DM the vendor contact afterwards.

sre-bot: Reminder: schedule follow-up post-call in #eng-sre, tag jin_ops and michael_k.

anita: Thanks everyone. Last check — any red lines?

jin_ops: Red line: no hard caps that prevent cross-region failover.

lucas_fin: Red line: no monthly visibility into invoice line items.

michael_k: Red line: inability to swap SKUs across families.

anita: Great — meeting at 10am PT. I'll attach the draft ask to the calendar invite.
